programs.title: The Darkside
programs.desc: Director Warwick Thornton assembles a collection of poignant, sad, funny, and absurd true ghost stories from across Australia with some of Australia's most iconic actors as the storytellers.

programs.title: Another Country
programs.desc: The great Aboriginal Australian actor David Dalaithngu tells the tale of 'Another Country', a story of what happened when his people's way of life was interrupted by ours.

programs.title: Ten Canoes
programs.desc: An elder of an Indigenous tribe in Australia's Northern territory realises a youngster on his first geese hunt is tempted to adultery with an elder brother's wife. Therefore he explains how traditionally the youth is told elaborate, edifying stories, like this one, since the earliest existence of the tribe, about how evil slips in, notably by sorcery, and ends up causing immense havoc unless prevented by virtue according to customary tribal law.

programs.title: Spear
programs.desc: Seeing the problems faced by Aboriginal men in remote and urban communities, a young Aboriginal man sets off on a journey of initiation to understand what it means to be a man in a modern-day world.

programs.title: The Black Hole
programs.desc: Aliens arrive, sparking bizarre, life-altering encounters in Estonia-featuring lust, spiders, and cosmic experiments. A surreal, witty tale blending sci-fi, sex, and satire from Estonian stories.

programs.title: Green Bush
programs.desc: Green Bush is a celebration of an era of music, working for the cause and getting things done. But not in the way you would expect.

programs.title: The Client
programs.desc: 11-year-old Mark Sway is torn between what he knows and what he can never tell. A hitman will kill Mark if the boy reveals what he knows about a Mob murder. Am ambitious federal prosecutor will keep the pressure on until Mark tells all. Mark is now a pawn in a deadly game, and his only ally is a courageous attorney who risks her career - and unexpectedly, her life - for him.

programs.title: Staring At Strangers
